headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, while LangGraph can read/write application files and expose stdin/stdout. With no documented isolation between them, content passed through shared files or tool outputs can be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default orchestration, though not proven to be directly automatic.
conditions: IF Flowise writes attacker-controlled content into a shared file or datastore that LangGraph later reads as prompt text
IF LangGraph forwards file or stdout content into a node that interprets it as instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Disable file-based handoff between the two flows
Add provenance tags to every inter-agent payload
Require a human review step before any prompt-like content is reused
requires-engineering: enforce content-type validation at the orchestration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and have broad model-provider egress, so data placed in shared workspace or chatflow state can flow into either backend. Flowise explicitly handles model provider keys and tool credentials, and LangGraph handles model provider API keys. This creates a default-path leakage risk for sensitive inputs and secrets across the pair.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, datastore, or uploaded files
IF either agent sends file contents or state to a remote model provider
mitigations: Use separate credentials for each agent
Keep secrets out of shared files and chatflow state
Restrict uploads to non-sensitive test data
Turn off unnecessary logging of prompts and tool outputs
requires-engineering: add per-agent encryption and access controls for shared state

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and shared server-datastore state across instances; LangGraph has write_filesystem plus persistent checkpointer-backed shared state. That overlapping mutable access creates a real conflict path, and the profiles do not show locking or coordination. Uncertainty about deployment isolation should be treated as higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, database, or checkpointer store
IF concurrent runs modify the same workflow artifacts without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate writable directory
Use distinct databases or checkpointer namespaces
Serialize writes with an external lock
Avoid concurrent edits to shared workflow artifacts
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder and LangGraph is a graph orchestration framework, so one agent’s output can readily become the other’s input. Neither profile shows a verification gate, and LangGraph can execute developer-defined tools, making unverified outputs dangerous when they drive actions. The interaction is documented only at the category level, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Flowise-generated text is consumed by a LangGraph node as authoritative state
IF LangGraph uses that state to trigger tools, API calls, or writes without validation
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require structured schemas for inter-agent messages
Log and diff every handoff payload
Block direct tool execution from untrusted upstream text
requires-engineering: add policy checks before any action-taking node

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications, residency limits, or retention policies. The main compliance issue is operational: if the pair is used on sensitive data, the shared file/state and broad egress can create policy mismatches. Because no specific residency or certification conflict is documented, this remains a low-confidence, low-severity compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through shared files or remote model providers
IF an operator requires residency, retention, or certification guarantees not stated in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Document retention and deletion expectations
Use separate environments for sensitive and non-sensitive runs
Review vendor terms before deployment
requires-engineering: add compliance controls and audit logging
